meta.strategy: Atraxa is a four-color (WUBG) proliferate deck: ramp early, then stack proliferate triggers on planeswalkers, poison counters and +1/+1 counters. Cheap removal, a few sweepers and card draw keep the table in check while the proliferate engine pushes toward poison or planeswalker value.

Kestia is the Bant enchantress commander, so the deck casts many enchantments and bestow creatures to draw cards through enchantress effects while building a big enchanted attacker that draws more on each attack. Ramp, cheap removal, and Winds of Rath (which spares enchanted creatures) protect the board while enchanted threats close the game.

Muldrotha is a Sultai value engine: fill the graveyard with mill and self-mill effects, then recast a land and one permanent of each type from it every turn. The deck leans on sacrifice outlets, ETB creatures, cheap ramp and removal to grind value, with budget-friendly lands for mana.

Kestia is a Bant enchantress deck: cast cheap enchantments and bestow creatures to trigger draw engines, then enchant a creature so every attack draws a card. Ramp, counterspells, spot removal and Winds of Rath protect enchanted creatures while the rest of the board gets cleared.

Muldrotha in Sultai: ramp and self-mill fill the graveyard, then each turn replay a land and one permanent of each type from it. Recursive value creatures, edicts and cheap removal grind out opponents, and the budget goes to Sol Ring, fixing and card advantage.

Muldrotha is a Sultai value engine that mills and self-fills the graveyard, then replays a land and one permanent of each type from it every turn. The deck runs cheap recursive creatures, ramp, sacrifice outlets, removal and Muldrotha-friendly draw while staying well under budget.

Mono-red Goblin tribal: deploy cheap Goblins and token makers, then tap Krenko, Mob Boss to double the Goblin count each turn. Sacrifice outlets, anthems and drain effects like Impact Tremors and Goblin Bombardment turn the swarm into a win, while ramp, draw and removal keep the engine running.

Atraxa is a four-color proliferate deck: ramp with rocks and land fetch, draw with proliferate spells, and add counter synergy plus a light poison plan. Cheap interaction and a few sweepers keep the table in check while the end-step proliferate grows planeswalkers and counters.

Mono-red Goblin tribal: deploy cheap Goblins and token makers so Krenko doubles the board every turn, supported by Warchief haste, Impact Tremors drain and Bombardment as a sacrifice outlet. Ramp, a few draw effects, burn removal and Blasphemous Act round it out, with cheap staples to stay in budget.

Mono-red Goblin tribal: tap Krenko each turn to double the Goblin count, supported by cheap Goblin tokens, lords, and haste enablers. Win with a huge Goblin swarm, Impact Tremors-style pings, Goblin War Strike and Bombardment, using cheap ramp, sweepers and burn for control.

Atraxa proliferate shell in four colors: cheap rocks and land fetch for ramp, cantrips that proliferate for card flow, and cheap proliferating flyers and toxic creatures to build poison. Budget removal and three cheap wraths protect the board while counters accumulate, and the rest of the mana comes from cheap taplands.

Build a Golgari elf tribal deck that ramps with mana elves, floods the board with Elf Warrior tokens and anthems, then drains with Lathril's ten-Elf tap ability. Cheap removal, a few wipes that spare Elves, and draw effects keep it running within budget.

Mono-blue spellslinger: cheap cantrips, counterspells and bounce each trigger Talrand for a stream of 2/2 flying Drakes, while cost reducers and card-draw engines keep the chain going. Counters and bounce protect the board until the Drake army swings in the air.

Mono-blue spellslinger: cheap cantrips, counterspells and cost reducers fuel Talrand's Drake tokens, while a few flyers and anthem effects turn the Drakes into a fast clock. Bounce and counters keep opponents off balance until the Drake army and the extra card draw close out the game.

Mono-blue spellslinger: cheap cantrips, counterspells and bounce trigger Talrand's Drakes, while cost reducers and draw engines keep the chain going. Win by flooding the board with flying Drakes and Birds backed by Favorable Winds, protected by counters.

Go wide with a dense Elf tribal core of mana elves, anthems and token makers, then use Lathril's menace and Elf Warrior tokens to fuel the tap-ten drain, or finish with Overrun effects. Cheap removal, a few wipes and draw engines keep the budget under $148.55 while staying consistent.

Flood the board with Elves and Elf Warrior tokens, using mana elves and anthems, then win through Lathril's menace combat tokens, the 10-Elf drain, or a Craterhoof-style alpha strike. Draw from Elf engines, protect the team with Boots and Greaves, and keep removal and sweepers that spare Elves.

Mass-produce cheap Vampires with Edgar's Eminence and lords like Stromkirk Captain and Legion Lieutenant. Then attack with Edgar to grow the team with counters and drain opponents with the life-loss pieces, backed by cheap removal and two sweepers that spare Vampires.

Grist makes Insect tokens every turn, fills the graveyard with mill, and uses sacrifice outlets and recursion to turn creatures into removal and a late-game drain. The deck pairs cheap ramp with graveyard-matters creatures, then relies on Hornet Queen, Scute Swarm and reanimation to overwhelm the table. Estimated spend is about $48.80 of the $49.59 limit.

Go wide with Vampire lords, tokens and drain, using Edgar's Eminence and attack trigger to grow the team. Cheap removal, cheap ramp and cheap card draw support the plan, and Olivia's Wrath, Kindred Judgment and Ruinous Ultimatum reset the board while the Vampires survive.

Go wide with a dense Vampire tribal package in Mardu colors, using Edgar's Eminence triggers and anthem lords like Captivating Vampire, Legion Lieutenant and Bloodline Keeper to grow the team. Edgar's attack triggers and drain effects like Blood Artist and Falkenrath Noble close the game, backed by cheap removal, wipes that spare Vampires, and plenty of ramp and draw (about $202 total).

Grist makes Insect tokens and mills itself, so we fill the yard with creatures and use Insect swarm payoffs, sacrifice outlets and recursion. Budget picks skip pricey staples for cheap ramp, removal, graveyard recursion and efficient lands, keeping the total near $60.

Make Insect tokens with Grist's +1 and fill the graveyard with creatures through self-mill. Then sacrifice the tokens for value, recur threats, and use Grist's -5 and the drain effects to close the game.

Esika is a five-color legendary-matters commander that ramps with mana rocks, uses its upkeep trigger to flip creatures and planeswalkers onto the battlefield, and fills the deck with legendary gods, planeswalkers and mana-fixing lands. Cheap ramp, removal, wipes and a few draw engines support the plan while staying well under budget.

Esika ramps with cheap any-color mana rocks and land fetch, then flips a creature or planeswalker onto the battlefield every upkeep. The budget fillers lean on legendary and planeswalker synergy, sweepers like Urza's Ruinous Blast that spare legendary permanents, and cheap removal.

Karn is a colorless artifact-ramp commander: flood the board with cheap artifacts and mana rocks, and use the upkeep colorless mana (artifact spells only) to cast big artifact finishers like Colossi, Wurmcoil and Myr Battlesphere. Cost reducers, Urza lands and Forsaken Monument speed things up, while artifact removal and a few sweepers keep control.

Esika is a five-color commander that fixes mana and flips a creature or planeswalker onto the battlefield each upkeep. The deck pairs cheap rocks and land ramp with legendary creatures and planeswalkers, and runs wipes that spare legendaries and planeswalkers (Urza's Ruinous Blast, Elspeth) plus cheap interaction and fixing lands, all within budget.

Karn is a colorless artifact deck that adds one mana per artifact each upkeep, so we play cheap mana rocks, artifact-cost reducers, and big colorless artifact finishers like Wurmcoil, Myr Battlesphere and Darksteel Colossus. Colorless removal and sweepers cover interaction while Urza lands and utility lands fill the mana base, all within budget.

Colorless artifact ramp: Sol Ring, rocks and Myr stack artifacts so Karn's upkeep trigger makes lots of artifact-only mana. That mana pays for big colorless finishers like Darksteel Colossus, Myr Battlesphere and Metalwork Colossus, backed by colorless removal and Nevinyrral's Disk.
